title: A cloned constant-state sub shares the prototype's CvXSUBANY SV without taking a reference
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 17535c984a (17535c984ae7d68304cc6e7b997240683f7fcadf) (2024-04-18). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin pad.c:2223 CvXSUBANY(cv) = CvXSUBANY(proto) with no SvREFCNT_inc; freed at pad.c:475). Host ASan at the pin: no ASan report; the workload's own oracle fails (rc=0); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sysalloc-sublet.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: no report: completes; with revocation off (_RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1) the same binary gives: no report: completes

status: all three Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
allocator_layer: nested allocator: the SV head arena (the CvXSUBANY const SV)
distinguishing: THE case the nested allocator buys, and the one case CheriBSD cannot catch. The CvXSUBANY SV head lives in Perl's own head arena: Perl recycles it on PL_sv_root and it never reaches free(), so an allocator-boundary scheme has nothing to revoke. CheriBSD is clean with revocation both off and on, host ASan is silent, and protecting the system allocator spatially AND temporally does not help either -- sysalloc-sublet is clean too, and it catches exactly what CheriBSD catches. Only Perl's own 'Attempt to free unreferenced scalar' and the SV head adapter report it. It is the whole argument for the third arm, in one case
note: NOT a quarantine-timing effect, measured rather than argued. CheriBSD's shadow bitmap gives one bit per 16-byte granule, set while quarantined, so membership is readable in O(1) without running a sweep. Under default revocation this case does 4072 mallocs and 2983 frees, ALL 2983 land in the quarantine -- so the quarantine is fully active -- and ZERO mallocs come back with the bit still set. Had the head travelled free() -> malloc(), it would either have been reissued while quarantined (counted, and the count is 0) or been swept first, which would have revoked the stale capability and faulted. Neither happened, so the head never crossed the allocator boundary at all. The probe is controlled in both directions: a freed block reads 1 and a live one 0 with revocation on, and a freed block reads 0 with revocation off
